'''Abdullah Omar Nasseef''' ({{langx|ar|عبد الله بن عمر نصيف}}; 5 July 1939 – 12 October 2025) was a Saudi chemist and geologist. He served as Chief Scout of the [[Saudi Arabian Boy Scouts Association]], which he joined in 1956.<ref name=AON/>

== Early life and education ==
Nasseef was born in [[Jeddah]] on 5 July 1939. He had a PhD degree from [[Leeds University]] in the United Kingdom.<ref name=SALT/>

== Career ==
Nasseef was a professor at [[King Abdulaziz University]] in Jeddah. He was chairman of the [[World Muslim Congress]], chairman of the founding board of Sahm Al-Nour Trust, and Secretary General of [[Muslim World League]] from 1983 to 1993.<ref name="SALT">{{cite web|url=http://sahmalnour.info/lang-en/organizational-structure/the-founding-board/102-abdullah-umar-nasif.html|publisher=Sahm Al Nour Trust|accessdate=1 August 2013|title=Dr. Abdullah Umar Nasif}} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> He served as vice-president of the [[Consultative Assembly of Saudi Arabia]], President of [[King Abdul Aziz University]], and Secretary-General of the [[International Islamic Council for Da'wah and Relief]] (IICDR).

== Death ==
Nasseef died on 12 October 2025, at the age of 86.<ref>{{cite news |title=رحيل العالم والداعية عبدالله نصيف |url=https://www.okaz.com.sa/people-situations/na/2217351 |access-date=12 October 2025 |publisher=Okaz |date=12 October 2025}}</ref>

== Awards and recognitions ==
In 1983 Nasseef was awarded the ''[[Bronze Wolf]]'', the only distinction of the [[World Organization of the Scout Movement]], awarded by the [[World Scout Committee]] for exceptional services to world [[Scouting]].<ref name=AON>{{Cite web |url=http://drabdullahomarnasseef.org/ |title=Dr Adbullah Omar Nasseef |access-date=28 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080323083602/http://drabdullahomarnasseef.org/ |archive-date=23 March 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.themwl.org/Bodies/Members/default.aspx?d=1&mid=4&l=AR World Muslim League] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725153440/http://www.themwl.org/Bodies/Members/default.aspx?d=1&mid=4&l=AR |date=25 July 2011 }}</ref>

Dr. Naseef was also awarded with the King Faisal Prize for Service to Islam in 1991 and the King Abdulaziz Medal of the First Class in 2004.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ummid.com/news/2025/october/13-10-2025/when-malegaon-rolled-out-red-carpet-for-dr-abdullah-omar-naseef.html | title=When Malegaon rolled out red carpet for Dr. Abdullah Omar Naseef | work=ummid.com | date=October 2025 | accessdate=13 October 2025}}</ref>
